title: A MASTERCLASS – Setting your clown free – Peredur Centre, East Grinstead, UK
body_html:
with Vivian Gladwell

An intensive week for advanced clowns limited to 6 participants. The course will enable each participant to explore in depth less familiar aspects of clowning with the intention of freeing their clown’s playfulness, creativity and risk taking.

This means one-to-one improvisations with feedback for each participant.

Possible areas of exploration are:

  • Rhythm
  • The clown’s relation to role and character
  • Working with paradox and conflict
  • Working with the audience
  • Acting versus not acting
  • Authenticity 
  • Pleasure
  • The Narrative structure
  • Chaos
  • The subversive clown
  • Surrealism and the absurd
  • Tragedy
  • Poetry
  • … and other discoveries

Prerequisites for the course are Clown level 1 and 2. 

Facilitator:

Vivian Gladwell 

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.

Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with theBataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).

He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.
He continues his role as ambassador for the work by researching the applications of clowning in the context of teacher training, medicine, conflict management, ecology and intercultural work in many countries (South Africa, USA, Senegal, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Italy, Germany, Norway…)

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

title: CLOWN AND DANCE- Peredur Centre – UK
body_html:
A weekend Clown, Movement and Dance Improvisation workshop.

OPEN TO ALL

In movement and physicality, we deepen the clowns commitment to both the here and now and the to world of the imagination.  This course invites you to make some playful and surprising discoveries for your clown as you immerse yourself in both movement and clown improvisation.  Find freedom in moving to the beat of your own drum without any steps to learn or routines to follow.  The clown always dances as if no-one is watching! Let’s play and explore the beautiful quirky and poetic dimension of the clown.

No previous movement or dance experience required.

THROUGH Clowning
We connect to our playful spirit. We develop and sustain in ourselves and each other the courage to be who we truly are, to trust life and ourselves. We befriend the fears that block us from being fully present in the here and now. The path of the Clown is simple, vulnerable and naive reminding us to dance lightly through life.

ABOUT Clowning

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us.

 

ABOUT Dance

Dance is for everybody: If you can move, you can dance!
Through dance improvisation, we learn to listen, and allow our dances to emerge organically from within ourselves. We never know what we are going to create, and that is precisely the point! There are no right or wrong ways to move and no steps to learn or remember – every dance is unique. Leaning on exercises developed by Barbara Mettler, we become more aware of the inner impulses that give rise to our movements. When we dance as individuals we listen to our bodies, giving form to what we feel inside. When we dance together, we surrender that individuality so we can listen to the ‘group body’, giving form to what we feel as a collective.

ABOUT Mettler based dance
Believing that dance is a basic human need, Barbara Mettler (1907 – 2002) explored new approaches to both the body as instrument and movement as the material of the dance. Her way of working emphasised individual and group improvisation as a means of cultivating the natural, creative movement resources which are in everyone. Mettler’s pioneering research, exploration and practice of large group dance improvisation is recognised as a ground breaking and unique contribution to contemporary dance. For more information on Mettler Based dance:https://dancecreative.org

Facilitators:

Ali Stockford – Clowning

Ali has been facilitating with Nose to Nose workshops for eight years and holds this work in high esteem as the perfect grounding for all creative work, developing our potential for full self-expression and the bigger picture of trusting ourselves and life and the power of fun!  As a member of the Nose to Nose Team, UK, she has delivered clown training for the Giggle Doctors, Theodora Foundation, UK,  Lis’n Tell Speech and Language practitioners and Quantum Marketing, London.  Ali grew up dancing – ballet, modern and tap -appearing in lots of musicals and pantos . She worked as a tap dancer in France alongside studying for a French literature degree and co-produced a one woman clown show – The Princess and the Pea- for children.  She is currently grappling with writing another clown piece which could transform into either a short story, film, or book or merely get left on the shelf until another time!  Ali speaks both English and French.

 

Beth Maiden – Movement and Dance Improvisation

Beth has always enjoyed dancing, but fell in love with movement improvisation in her 30s. At first practicing solo and in secret (“what is this weird thing I love to do?”) and then finding the courage to move with others (“wow, it’s even better when we do it together!”)

She is fascinated by the the magic that happens when we allow our bodies to move and communicate without judgement. Sometimes silly, sometimes profound, often both, Beth believes dance and movement are powerful ways to listen to those parts of ourselves that don’t get heard in everyday life.

Beth now considers dance improvisation central to her life and wellbeing, and is continually seeking out new approaches to dance to deepen her understanding of this practice. Among others she has studied with Nose to Nose, the School of Disobedience and Cai Tomos, as well as teacher training with Mettler Studios in the US.

8-10 January 2027

A Weekend introduction to Reimagining the World Through Play

This weekend workshop brings together the principles of Doughnut Economics and the practice of social clowning.
Doughnut Economics asks one of the great questions of our time: how can we create a world in which everyone has enough to live well, without pushing the planet beyond its limits? Clowning brings another kind of intelligence to this question — embodied, relational, imaginative and full of surprise.
Over the weekend, we will explore some of the seven ways of thinking like a 21st-century economist through clowning, movement, improvisation, archetype and performance. We will not approach these ideas as experts. We will let go of needing to know, explain or persuade. Instead, we will begin from clown ground: presence, listening, openness, vulnerability and the pleasure of being changed by what happens.
This workshop is suitable for people with or without clowning experience, and for people with or without prior knowledge of Doughnut Economics. It will be especially relevant for artists, educators, facilitators, activists, community workers, sustainability practitioners and anyone looking for a more joyful way to engage with the challenges of our time.
12-16 participants – 220 gbp

Kate Raworth

Her internationally best-selling book Doughnut Economics: seven ways to think like a 21st century economist has been translated into over 20 languages and has been widely influential with diverse audiences, from the UN General Assembly to Pope Francis to Extinction Rebellion.

Kate is a Senior Teaching Fellow at Oxford University’s Environmental Change Institute, where she teaches on the Masters in Environmental Change and Management. She is also Professor of Practice at Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences.

Over the past 25 years, Kate’s career has taken her from working with micro-entrepreneurs in the villages of Zanzibar to co-authoring the Human Development Report for UNDP in New York, followed by a decade as Senior Researcher at Oxfam.

She holds a first class BA in Politics, Philosophy and Economics, and an MSc in Economics for Development, both from Oxford University. She has been awarded honorary doctorates by the University of York, University College Dublin, KU Leuven, and Business School Lausanne. She is also a member of the Club of Rome and Honorary Fellow of the Royal Academy of the Arts.

Kate has written extensively for media including The Guardian, The New Statesman, Newsweek.com, and Wired.com, and has contributed to many radio programmes including for BBC Radio 4, The World Service, ABC and NPR, as well as television including CNN World News, Al-Jazeera, BBC, ITV and CBC. Her 2018 TED talk has over 5 million views.

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.
Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).

title: COURAGE TO BE – A 4 DAY COURSE ON BARDSEY ISLAND / YNYS ENLII, WALES
body_html:
WITH TOBY SPAVEN and ALI STOCKFORD

We are delighted to offer four playful days of clowning on the beautiful Ynys Enlli—a place of wild beauty, sea air, seals and Manx shearwaters. Enjoy locally sourced delicious vegetarian food and stay in one of the islands 1870”s houses.

The word courage comes from a root meaning “heart.” Through clowning and reconnecting with our playful spirit, we can develop and sustain — in ourselves and each other — the heart to be who we truly are, to trust life and to trust ourselves. Taking heart is a profoundly inward process: an invitation to soften the fears that keep us guarded, and to become more fully present in ourselves and what is around us.

Island life has a stillness, a quietness and brings a shear sense of wander that helps us comes back to ourselves. Let the boat crossing shed any roles that you don’t need and gather to play, explore and discover together through games, exercises, short impros and moments of joyful foolishness designed to awaken your inner clown.

We’ll base our activities in our Clown Hideaway and uncover natural stages across the island—on cliff paths, in fields, by the sea. We’ll listen, respond and play with the island itself as our inspiration. There will be voice work on the beach accompanied by the choruses of seals, gentle ensemble work, laughter, stlliness, surprise and space to reconnect with the pleasure of being gloriously human.

Whether you are completely new to clowning or already travelling alongside your clown, this is an invitation to play deeply, fail beautifully and discover what happens when clown meets wilderness.

ABOUT CLOWNING

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us. Come for a weekend of letting go and freeing up!
The group is limited to 14.

 

 

Facilitators:

Toby Spaven 

Toby is a drag artist, and dancer and works as a builder by day.  They have been training with nose to nose as a clown facilitator and has been transformed by the nose to nose courses. They facilitate groups in the construction and sports industry to build trust and vulnerability within the working and playing culture. They love to play.

Toby has had the fortune to be involved in the building maintenance on Ynys Enlli and fell in love with the island as soon as they stepped off the boat.

 

 

Alison Stockford (Ali) 

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning workshops since 2016, teaching across the UK and, more recently, Europe. She holds this work in high esteem as the perfect grounding for all creative work exploring the power of fun, connection  and our shared human experience as well as developing theatrical awareness

Drawn to what is authentically funny, moving, and true in each individual, Ali enjoys creating welcoming spaces where people can step into the present moment, take creative risks, and embrace a playful way of being.

A qualified teacher (Université de Lille, France, and the University of Reading, UK), Ali is a former Head of Performing Arts at St Mary’s Special School and College, Bexhill, and is fluent in English and French.

Alongside leading Nose to Nose Clowning Levels 1–5, she has delivered training for the Giggle Doctors at Theodora Foundation, Lis’n Tell Speech and Language Practitioners, Quantum Marketing, and medical students at the University of Bristol. She has also worked as a social clown and facilitator at events including The Imaginarium, ARU Cambridge’s Writers’ Conference, and the ANTITHESES Conference at St Hilda’s College, Oxford.

title: COURAGE TO BE – CLOWN 1 -A FIVE DAY WORKSHOP, CENTRAL LONDON
body_html:
with Vivian Gladwell and Ali Stockford

The word “courage” comes from a root that means “heart.” Through clowning and connecting to our playful spirit we can develop and sustain, in ourselves and each other, the heart to be who we truly are, to trust life and ourselves. “Taking heart” is a profoundly inward process, and an invitation for overcoming the fears that block us from being fully present in the “Here and Now.” This course establishes the ground for all our work and is an essential first step before going on to more advanced courses.
The group is limited to 12

“Nose to Nose is a transformative experience! The gentleness, generosity and care surrounding the playing and clowning makes it such a safe and exhilarating experience. I always leave these workshops feeling like a better person. I am becoming a happier and more confident clown and it is thanks to this special way of working. I can’t wait to be back.” Astrid Olofsson- Actress

Facilitators:

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.
Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).
He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.
He continues his role as ambassador for the work by researching the applications of clowning in the context of teacher training, medicine, conflict management, ecology and intercultural work in many countries (South Africa, USA, Senegal, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Italy, Germany, Norway…)

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

  Alison Stockford

Alison (Ali) Stockford – Clowning

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning workshops since 2016, teaching across the UK and, more recently, Europe. She holds this work in high esteem as the perfect grounding for all creative work exploring the power of fun, connection  and our shared human experience as well as developing theatrical awareness. Drawn to what is authentically funny, moving, and true in each individual, Ali enjoys creating welcoming spaces where people can step into the present moment, take creative risks, and embrace a playful way of being.

A qualified teacher (Université de Lille, France, and University of Reading, UK), Ali is a former Head of Performing Arts at St Mary’s Special School and College, Bexhill, and is fluent in English and French.

Alongside co-facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning Levels 1–5, she has delivered training for the Giggle Doctors at Theodora Foundation, Lis’n Tell Speech and Language Practitioners, Quantum Marketing, and medical students at the University of Bristol. She has also worked as a social clown and facilitator at events including The Imaginarium, ARU Cambridge’s Writers’ Conference, and the ANTITHESES Conference at St Hilda’s College, Oxford.

Facilitators:

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.
Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).

January 15-17, 2027
with Vivian Gladwell and Abigail Dancey 

“To feel abandoned is to deny the intimacy of your surroundings…
Surely, even you, at times, have felt the grand array;
the swelling presence, and the chorus, crowding out your solo voice.
You must note the way the soap dish enables you,
or the window latch grants you freedom.
Alertness is the hidden discipline of familiarity.
The stairs are your mentor of things to come,
the doors have always been there to frighten you and invite you,
and the tiny speaker in the phone is your dream-ladder to divinity.”

– David Whyte, Everything is Waiting For You

Course description:
Clowns are shapeshifters, able to transform themselves by playfully interpreting the word around them. They can help us to shift our perspectives and awaken empathy by bringing the world alive.

In this unique course, we will guide you through practical exercises and simple improvisational structures to help you cultivate your skills and deepen your understanding of the art of clowning. 

Identification with objects teaches important clowning principles such as:

  • commitment to physicality and embodiment,
  • use of voice for emotional expression,
  • relationship with partners and audience,
  • personal freedom
  • breaking the rules of theatrical convention
  • exploring roles and breaking free from roles 

Come play and let your clown discover the world as new and full of opportunity, absurdity, laughter and poignancy. 

This weekend is open to all levels – whether you’re experienced or new to clowning. 

The group is limited to 12 people.

Formateur dans les stages du Bataclown (formation de base et formation certifiante “clown et intervention sociale”, coresponsable pédagogique de la filière “Secteur événementiel” ).

![Bertil Sylvander](https://www.bataclown.com/local/cache-vignettes/L350xH230/arton981-a98c1.jpg?1732687055)Il a travaillé le théâtre et l’improvisation, le masque, le mime, la commedia dell’arte, la voix, le clown, le bouffon et le fou du roi avec la Cie “Le Fil à Plomb” (Christian Cailleret), la Cie “Omnibus” (méthode Decroux), Serge Martin, Georges Bonnaud, Hervé Laudières, le Roy Hart Théâtre, etc. Il a travaillé le piano et la clarinette. Gymnastique sensorielle méthode Danis Bois depuis 2006.  
Il a joué dans les spectacles du “Rateau Bavoir” (Fanfare clownesque) de 1978 à 80 et du Bataclown (depuis 1980).

WITH ALI STOCKFORD and ALEXIA ELLIOTT

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us. Come for a weekend of letting go and freeing up!
The group is limited to 14.

Facilitators:

Alison Stockford

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose workshops for over ten years for creatives and people from all walks of life who are interested in exploring this extraordinary character and archetype. She sees clown improvisation as the perfect grounding for all creative work, developing our potential for full self-expression and the bigger picture of trusting ourselves and life.  A member of the Nose to Nose Team, UK, Clown facilitation has also taken her into training work for the Giggle Doctors, Theodora Foundation, UK and for Lis’n Tell Speech and Language practitioners UK.  Previous work includes devising and directing performance with young people and adults with learning disabilities and as a performer and tap dancer in street theatre, school tours and cabaret with companies Inside Out Theatre Company and Les Amuse-Gueules, France.

avec Vivian Gladwell
samedi 7 nov au dimanche 8 nov 2026

Que se passe-t-il si nous approchons le conflit avec le nez rouge ?

Durant ce week-end, nous explorerons de manière ludique et sensible comment le clown peut nous aider à transformer notre rapport au conflit. Inspiré par L’imagination morale de John Paul Lederach, ce stage propose de rencontrer tensions, désaccords et oppositions non comme des impasses, mais comme des espaces de créativité, de relation et de découverte.

Le clown nous invite à ralentir, à écouter, à ne pas savoir trop vite, à rester en contact avec ce qui est là — même quand c’est inconfortable, absurde ou fragile. Par le jeu, l’improvisation, le corps et la présence, nous chercherons ensemble d’autres façons d’habiter le conflit : avec plus de souplesse, d’humanité, d’humour et d’imagination.

Un week-end pour explorer avec profondeur et légèreté,
pour rire, rater, recommencer,
et pour laisser émerger des réponses inattendues là où, d’habitude, nous nous fermons.

Réservez votre place dès maintenant et laissez votre esprit clownesque s’épanouir dans un monde d’émotions et d’audace.

Le groupe est limité à 12 personnes

Formateur:

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian est le fondateur et directeur de Nose to Nose. Il a donné des centaines d’ateliers à travers le monde. Il vit à la fois au Royaume-Uni et en France où il a commencé à faire le clown en Il parle couramment le français et l’anglais.

Vivian a commencé à enseigner en 1988 dans le cadre du Lifeways Festival à Emerson College – Royaume-Uni. Il a suivi une formation de facilitateur avec le Bataclown en 1990 et a rejoint leur équipe en 1991, travaillant également comme bouffon des temps modernes (clownanalyste). Il a créé Nose to Nose UK en 1990, Nose to Nose Amérique du Nord en 2006 et Fool View, un groupe de Social Clowning. Il a formé des animateurs au Royaume-Uni, aux États-Unis, en Allemagne et en Italie – voir l’historique.

Il poursuit son rôle d’ambassadeur du travail en recherchant les applications du clown dans le contexte de la formation des enseignants, de la médecine, de la gestion des conflits, de l’écologie et du travail interculturel dans de nombreux pays (Afrique du Sud, USA, Sénégal, Vietnam, Inde, Malaisie, Italie, Allemagne, Norvège…).

body_html:
With Ali Stockford

This November try something new with a one day workshop in Nose to Nose Clowning. This will be a light-hearted, playful day exploring creativity, connection and spontaneity whilst discovering the poetry and the funny of the Clown.

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us. Come for a day of letting go and freeing up!

The group is limited to 12

Facilitator : Alison (Ali) Stockford

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning workshops since 2016, teaching across the UK and more recently Europe. She sees this work as a strong practical foundation for creative practice, focusing on play, connection and presence while developing theatrical awareness. Interested in what is genuinely funny, touching and true for each person, Ali enjoys creating spaces where people can meet the moment simply, playfully and together. A qualified teacher (Université de Lille, France & University of Reading, UK), Ali is a fluent English–French speaker and former Head of Performing Arts at St Mary’s Special School and College, Bexhill. She has led Nose to Nose Clowning trainings (Levels 1–5) all over the UK and beyond, and worked with everyone from Giggle Doctors and medical students to writers, marketers and speech & language practitioners.

with Vivian Gladwell and Ali Stockford

The course offers a practical exploration of the clown’s take on biographical stories.

From 2027, this course is now limited to a maximum of 8 participants.

What is Social Clowning? 
Social Clowning is the use of clowning and play as a way of revealing multiple ways of making sense of the stories we tell. The clown archetype touches on:

  • Authenticity 
  • Vulnerability 
  • Empowerment 
  • Truth
  • Courage
  • Imagination
  • Integrating our shadow
  • Expressing needs
  • Listening
  • Self-expression

The absurd reflection of ourselves and of the world that the clown offers us puts the human heart back at the very centre of our lives.

The group is limited to 8 participants.

PRE-REQUISITE: This course requires participants to have done Clown 1, 2, 3.

Facilitator: Vivian Gladwell and Ali Stockford

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.
Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).
He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

 

Alison (Ali) Stockford

Performing experience includes: tap dancer and comedy actor in café-théâtre with Les Amuses Gueules Lille, France; Street Theatre and Theatre in Education with Inside Out Theatre Company, Hastings. title: THE HEART AND CLOWN- Hastings- UK
body_html:
6th and 7th February 2027
A weekend workshop in Dance and Clowning 

An exploration of  movement, dance, imagination and the red nose.

OPEN TO ALL

During this weekend workshop, Emma and Ali will lead you on a journey that weaves the poetic worlds of Dance and Clown Improvisation.

Our theme: The Heart.

No previous movement, dance or clowning experience required. This course is for beginners and more experienced alike.

 

About the Dance

The hearts dance of vulnerability.
Finding shape and metaphor of our heart as we move into the landscape of the unknown .
Daring , taking risks , stepping out beyond what we think we know about ourselves . Improvised movement and dance held in the map of the 5Rhythms .
What cautionary tales do we have to share?  The body doesn’t lie, the dancer reveals us to ourselves, the heart leads the way.

About the Clowning.

What is it about the Clown that touches our hearts? The Clowns ability to live authentically, and to wear their heart on their sleeve endears us to this optimistic character. In failing joyfully, the Clown lets us know that it is ok to make mistakes, fall down and break rules –  and that the important thing is that we remain connected to the present moment and to each other.  In play, we remember that is possible to navigate the world with lightness of heart.  Expect games, exercises and short improvisations to explore this heart oriented practice.

“It was brilliant – so much fun, it’s brought me joy, silliness and buoyancy into the days afterwards too. Thank you both!” R – previous participant

 

More info:

The 5 Rhythms is a  embodied improvised freedom of movement practice. Living in each moment, surrendering to instinct and following the language of metaphor as it unravels us into our unique dance.

There are no steps to learn, the choreography is alive in each moment without planning, responding to the music, physically expressing with spontaneity.
The 5 Rhythms Flowing Staccato Chaos Lyrical and Stillness are the map we follow, energy in motion creating a wave like pattern that guide us.

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us.

Through Clowning we connect to our playful spirit. We develop and sustain in ourselves and each other the courage to be who we truly are, to trust life and ourselves. We befriend the fears that block us from being fully present in the here and now. The path of the Clown is simple, vulnerable and naive reminding us to dance lightly through life.

THE JOY OF BREAKING RULES

A joyful, challenging and liberating five days for anyone ready to discover the wisdom of the fool, the pleasure of getting it wrong, and the unexpected beauty of breaking rules.

with Andreas L. Maier and Vivian Gladwell

Wednesday 11.11.2026 18h-21h
Thur-Sat 12.11.-14.11.2026 10h-18h
Sunday 15.11.2026 10h-13h

Where
50678 Cologne, Germany (close to Chlodwigplatz/Südstadt)

Costs (sliding scale, see below)
580€ – 380€

Workshop language – English with possible translation in German. 

COURSE DESCRIPTION
What happens when we stop trying to be good and instead become playfully, innocently disobedient?

In clowning rules are everywhere — the rules of games, theatre, politeness, success, and how we think we should appear. The clown listens to them, tries to follow, and then fails, forgets, rebels or invents something more interesting. In breaking rules, the clown reveals what might live beneath them: fear, longing, mischief, tenderness, delight. When these are allowed to appear, the stage becomes more alive — and so do we.

This five‑day course invites you to explore the clown as a joyful rule‑breaker.

Through physical play, improvisation and simple performance structures, we’ll discover the freedom that comes from meeting our habits with curiosity and staying connected — to the audience, the group, the moment and to the deeper truth of what is happening.

This is not about being clever, anarchic, or funny on command. It is about discovering the freedom that comes when we meet our habits with curiosity. 

Over the five days we will explore:

  • the rules of games
    (and the pleasure of misunderstanding them)
  • the rules of objects
    (chairs, coats, doors, bags and other everyday conspirators)
  • the rules of social behaviour
    (politeness, status, embarrassment and permission)
  • the rules of performance
    (entrances, exits, endings, failure and applause)
  • the personal rules that limit our imagination
    (“I must be funny”, “I must get it right”, “I must not be too much”, “I must not be seen”)

This course is for people with some previous clowning or improvisation experience who wish to deepen their play, become more available on stage, and explore the comic and poetic possibilities of failure, freedom and disobedience.
The course is limited to 12 participants.

This workshop is offered on a sliding scale. This means there is a price range, and you choose where you place yourself on that scale, based on your current financial situation.

In our understanding, the sliding scale supports both access and fairness. It recognises that participants have different financial realities, while also valuing the time, care, and labour of the freelance facilitators who lead this workshop and rely on this work for their income. 

Our finances are shaped by many things—income, health, caring responsibilities, debt, and access to support. There is no income check. Vivian Gladwell
Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.

Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).

He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.

He continues his role as ambassador for the work by researching the applications of clowning in the context of teacher training, medicine, conflict management, ecology and intercultural work in many countries (South Africa, USA, Senegal, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Italy, Germany, Norway…)

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

Andreas L. Maier
Andreas has a degree in acting and works as a performer, artistic speaker, presenter and audio artist. Since 2006 he has been training young actors at universities, professional performers and offers numerous workshops and seminars on presence training and storytelling.

He studied at the Berlin University of the Arts and has worked at numerous municipal and state theatres in Germany, including the Maxim Gorki Theatre, Schauspiel Bonn and TuP Essen as well as the Schauspielhaus Bochum and the Opera House Dortmund.

He has been freelancing in DACH since 2006 and has performed with various independent groups and artistic collectives, e.g. kainkollektiv, Drama Köln and subbotnik. Since 2008 he has completed numerous further training courses, e.g. as a somatic movement teacher according to BMC ©, with voice training according to the Lichtenberg method and clown training with Nose to Nose. Currently he’s taking part in their ongoing clowning facilitator training 2024-2026.

Andreas’ work as a performer has received several awards since 1998. He lives in Cologne and speaks German and English fluently.

An introductory course for beginners.

Designed for complete beginners in clowning and for those new to Mettler Dance, there are no steps to master, no routines to memorise. Simply come as you are, with an open mind and a willingness to be curious.

Together we’ll slow down, listen, move and discover what emerges in the moment.

Through playful improvisation, movement, breath, connection, and imagination, you’ll begin to uncover both the dancer and the clown that already live within you.

Later, you’ll explore how these two creative worlds can meet—allowing movement to inspire play, and play to awaken movement. Expect moments of laughter, surprise, freedom, and genuine connection, all within a supportive and encouraging environment.

Whether you’re looking to reconnect with your creativity, experience the delight of improvisation, or simply try something completely new, this workshop offers a space to explore without judgement and discover the joy of responding to the present moment. We will be working in a light filled studio with wooden sprung floor.

For those who wish to continue the journey, this introductory workshop is followed by a deeper exploration for participants with more experience in Clowning and Mettler Dance improvisation.

No previous movement, dance  or clowning experience required.

 

THROUGH Clowning
We connect to our playful spirit. We develop and sustain in ourselves and each other the courage to be who we truly are, to trust life and ourselves. We befriend the fears that block us from being fully present in the here and now. The path of the Clown is simple, vulnerable and naive reminding us to dance lightly through life.

 

ABOUT Clowning

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us.

THROUGH Dance

Dance is for everybody: If you can move, you can dance!
Through dance improvisation, we learn to listen, and allow our dances to emerge organically from within ourselves. We never know what we are going to create, and that is precisely the point! There are no right or wrong ways to move and no steps to learn or remember – every dance is unique. Leaning on exercises developed by Barbara Mettler, we become more aware of the inner impulses that give rise to our movements. When we dance as individuals we listen to our bodies, giving form to what we feel inside. When we dance together, we surrender that individuality so we can listen to the ‘group body’, giving form to what we feel as a collective.

ABOUT Mettler based dance
Believing that dance is a basic human need, Barbara Mettler (1907 – 2002) explored new approaches to both the body as instrument and movement as the material of the dance. Her way of working emphasised individual and group improvisation as a means of cultivating the natural, creative movement resources which are in everyone. Mettler’s pioneering research, exploration and practice of large group dance improvisation is recognised as a ground breaking and unique contribution to contemporary dance. For more information on Mettler Based dance:https://dancecreative.org

Facilitators:

Ali Stockford – Clowning

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning workshops since 2016, teaching across the UK and, more recently, Europe. She holds this work in high esteem as the perfect grounding for all creative work exploring the power of fun, connection and our shared human experience as well as developing theatrical awareness.

Drawn to what is authentically funny, moving, and true in each individual, Ali enjoys creating welcoming spaces where people can step into the present moment, take creative risks, and embrace a playful way of being.

A qualified teacher (Université de Lille, France, and the University of Reading, UK), Ali is a former Head of Performing Arts at St Mary’s Special School and College, Bexhill, and is fluent in English and French.

Alongside leading Nose to Nose Clowning Levels 1–5, she has delivered clown training for the Giggle Doctors at Theodora Foundation, Lis’n Tell Speech and Language Practitioners, Quantum Marketing, and medical students at the University of Bristol. She has also worked as a social clown at events including The Imaginarium, ARU Cambridge’s Writers’ Conference, and the ANTITHESES Conference at St Hilda’s College, Oxford.

 

Beth Maiden – Movement and Dance Improvisation

Beth has always enjoyed dancing, but fell in love with movement improvisation in her 30s. At first practicing solo and in secret (“what is this weird thing I love to do?”) and then finding the courage to move with others (“wow, it’s even better when we do it together!”)

She is fascinated by the the magic that happens when we allow our bodies to move and communicate without judgement. Sometimes silly, sometimes profound, often both, Beth believes dance and movement are powerful ways to listen to those parts of ourselves that don’t get heard in everyday life.

Beth now considers dance improvisation central to her life and wellbeing, and is continually seeking out new approaches to dance to deepen her understanding of this practice. Among others she has studied with Nose to Nose, the School of Disobedience and Cai Tomos, as well as teacher training with Mettler Studios in the US.

title: THE WISDOM OF IMPERFECTION – CLOWN 3 – a six-day residential course
body_html:
NB THIS COURSE IS LIMITED TO 8 PARTICIPANTS.

Clowning is the art of making mistakes and there is an art to paying attention to the unexpected, to accidents and those unintended things we do. Sometimes our striving for perfection blinds us to what the world is trying to tell us. Great wisdom can be found in making peace with our shadows and our shortcomings and clowning celebrates all our humanity even those part of it we are desperately trying not to be.

This level III course brings a fresh new way of looking at impros by focusing on the many strategies we use for avoiding mistakes. The course gives a greater focus on theatrical and improvisational techniques and will feel very different from previous levels. For example, impros are repeated to bring actors to work in less familiar and/or comfortable areas.

Level 3 moves the work one step closer to performance and is an ideal preliminary to Towards Performance and/or Social Clowning.

Facilitators: 

Vivian Gladwell

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.
Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).
He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.
He continues his role as ambassador for the work by researching the applications of clowning in the context of teacher training, medicine, conflict management, ecology and intercultural work in many countries (South Africa, USA, Senegal, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Italy, Germany, Norway…)

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

Alison Stockford (Ali)

 

Facilitating  workshops with Nose to Nose since 2016,  Ali holds this work in high esteem as a perfect grounding for all creative work and the bigger picture of trusting ourselves and life.  Always on the lookout for what is authentically funny, touching and true to each individual, Ali enjoys creating spaces for peeps to step into the present moment in a playful and connected way.

Performing experience includes: tap dancer and comedy actor in café-théâtre with Les Amuses Gueules Lille, France; Street Theatre and Theatre in Education with Inside Out Theatre Company, Hastings. In addition to nearly 100 workshops for Nose to Nose, Ali has delivered trainings for the Giggle Doctors – Theodora Foundation, Lis’n Tell Speech and Language Practitioners, Quantum Marketing, London, medical students at the University of Bristol and  as a social clown at The Imaginarium, Cambridge and the ANTITHESES conference, St Hilda’s College, Oxford  Ali speaks both English and French.

title: WHEN TREES COULD SPEAK – Level 1 – An online course for discovering your Clown through Puppetry
body_html:
January 10 to February 14, 2027
An Online Course of 6 weekly sessions of 2 hours
With Vivian Gladwell and Laura Geilen

In this online course the screen becomes the perfect puppet stage – framing and focusing the play in a way that’s uniquely suited to clowning with puppets. Using puppets, the identities of clown, puppet and puppeteer blur, the conventions unravel, and the confusion becomes brilliant material for comedy and discovery.
This format invites deeper focus, bold creativity, and delightful chaos.

What can puppets teach us about reclaiming our human connection to each other and to our world?

For beginners as well as confirmed clowns or puppeteers this course is about finding freedom and discovering the many internal dialogues that we carry within us. We will explore the basics of clowning and comedy through improvisations with puppets. We will also look at making our own puppets out of simple everyday objects.

Puppetry is about making the world around us come alive and giving a voice to our innermost thoughts. See links about puppetry below.

The group is limited to 12 participants.

WHO IS THIS COURSE  FOR?
Anyone with an interest in discovering clowning and/or puppetry and how the two can enhance one another. Beginners and professionals alike are welcome. 

PREREQUISITES:
No prerequisites except for wifi access and a computer. Please let us know if you need technical help with Zoom.

COURSE DATES

body_html:
Where the Clown Appears

A 4 day advanced workshop in clown and dance impro.

Ready to take your clown into motion?

If you’ve completed  Clown 1-Courage to Be or a Level 1 Clown & Dance weekend, this is your invitation to go deeper.

We’ll dive further into Mettler Dance Improvisation, discovering new ways to move, listen, play and connect. We’ll explore new dance improvisations, with more opportunities for whole-group movement — allowing your own expression, impulses and creativity to flow.

No steps. No routines. No right way to move.
Just an openness to move, connect and discover what happens.

Where the clown appears: Dance can become a playful portal into the clown’s imagination — unlocking possibilities, surprises and connections.

Through unique clown improvisations that call on you to move and dance, you’ll have opportunities to set your clown into motion, develop presence and expand your clown’s movement repertoire.

Who is this for?

You’ll need to have completed Clown 1 – Courage to Be or an intro to Nose to Nose clowning  or a Level 1 Clown & Dance weekend.

THROUGH Clowning
We connect to our playful spirit. We develop and sustain in ourselves and each other the courage to be who we truly are, to trust life and ourselves. We befriend the fears that block us from being fully present in the here and now. The path of the Clown is simple, vulnerable and naive reminding us to dance lightly through life.

ABOUT Clowning

Clowning is a state of playfulness that brings us to experience a child-like, naïve and vulnerable state of being. Paradoxically we grow, learn and are strengthened through reconnecting playfully with what makes us most vulnerable. This approach to clowning is not a technique (tricks, gags and routines) but a personal journey towards finding one’s own unique way of being a clown, by listening and being receptive, essential skills for any creative and imaginative expression. It is only when we let go our control over things that we begin to be surprised by the depth of what reveals itself to us.

ABOUT Dance

Dance is for everybody: If you can move, you can dance!
Through dance improvisation, we learn to listen, and allow our dances to emerge organically from within ourselves. We never know what we are going to create, and that is precisely the point! There are no right or wrong ways to move and no steps to learn or remember – every dance is unique. Leaning on exercises developed by Barbara Mettler, we become more aware of the inner impulses that give rise to our movements. When we dance as individuals we listen to our bodies, giving form to what we feel inside. When we dance together, we surrender that individuality so we can listen to the ‘group body’, giving form to what we feel as a collective.

ABOUT Mettler based dance
Believing that dance is a basic human need, Barbara Mettler (1907 – 2002) explored new approaches to both the body as instrument and movement as the material of the dance. Her way of working emphasised individual and group improvisation as a means of cultivating the natural, creative movement resources which are in everyone. Mettler’s pioneering research, exploration and practice of large group dance improvisation is recognised as a ground breaking and unique contribution to contemporary dance. For more information on Mettler Based dance:https://dancecreative.org

Facilitators:

Ali Stockford – Clowning

Ali has been facilitating Nose to Nose Clowning workshops since 2016, teaching across the UK and, more recently, Europe. She holds this work in high esteem as the perfect grounding for all creative work exploring the power of fun, connection  and our shared human experience as well as developing theatrical awareness

Drawn to what is authentically funny, moving, and true in each individual, Ali enjoys creating welcoming spaces where people can step into the present moment, take creative risks, and embrace a playful way of being.

A qualified teacher (Université de Lille, France, and the University of Reading, UK), Ali is a former Head of Performing Arts at St Mary’s Special School and College, Bexhill, and is fluent in English and French.

Alongside leading Nose to Nose Clowning Levels 1–5, she has delivered training for the Giggle Doctors at Theodora Foundation, Lis’n Tell Speech and Language Practitioners, Quantum Marketing, and medical students at the University of Bristol. She has also worked as a social clown and facilitator at events including The Imaginarium, ARU Cambridge’s Writers’ Conference, and the ANTITHESES Conference at St Hilda’s College, Oxford.

 

Beth Maiden – Movement and Dance Improvisation

Beth has always enjoyed dancing, but fell in love with movement improvisation in her 30s. At first practicing solo and in secret (“what is this weird thing I love to do?”) and then finding the courage to move with others (“wow, it’s even better when we do it together!”)

She is fascinated by the the magic that happens when we allow our bodies to move and communicate without judgement. Sometimes silly, sometimes profound, often both, Beth believes dance and movement are powerful ways to listen to those parts of ourselves that don’t get heard in everyday life.

Beth now considers dance improvisation central to her life and wellbeing, and is continually seeking out new approaches to dance to deepen her understanding of this practice. Among others she has studied with Nose to Nose, the School of Disobedience and Cai Tomos, as well as teacher training with Mettler Studios in the US.

Vivian is the founder and director of Nose to Nose and has given hundreds of workshops around the world. He lives both in the UK and France where he started clowning in 1978. He speaks French and English fluently.

Vivian began teaching in 1988 as part of the Lifeways Festival at Emerson College – UK. He trained as a facilitator with the Bataclown in 1990 and joined their team in 1991 also working as a modern day Court Jester (Clownanalyst).

He created Nose to Nose UK in 1990, Nose to Nose of North America in 2006, Nose to Nose Germany in 2008, NTN Italy in 2016 and Fool View, the Social Clowning group and has trained facilitators in the UK, the USA, Germany and Italy – view history.
He continues his role as ambassador for the work by researching the applications of clowning in the context of teacher training, medicine, conflict management, ecology and intercultural work in many countries (South Africa, USA, Senegal, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Italy, Germany, Norway…)

He holds clowning as a social playground for exploring our humanity.

Sarah French

For as long as Sarah remembers, she has been interested in how people play. She had set out as a practicing psychotherapist when she stumbled into the paradoxical world of Clown, which set her on an enlivening path, despite her hesitations and fears. She has collaborated with Vivian Gladwell of Nose to Nose since 2012. Sarah considers that she has many teachers, including the spinner dolphins of Hawaii, who are the clowns of the sea.

In 2021, Sarah founded Fool Tree, a small center for the playful arts in Ghent, NY, where she continues to facilitate clowning workshops, transformational tarot, and other community events.
